title: ULC: Sequentially Train One Fine-Grained Loco-Manipulation Policy
content_lines: Source: [arXiv:2507.06905v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.06905v2). The official project still marked code as coming soon at the audit point; no third-party repository is treated as author code.

> **Bottom line:** ULC puts velocity, root height, torso orientation, and arm-joint targets into one policy, but activates them through a sequential curriculum. Programmed arm targets provide feedforward commands and the policy learns residual balance compensation.
## Engineering problem

When all whole-body objectives start together, easy velocity rewards can dominate precise torso/arm behavior. Directly learning absolute arm targets also discards useful operator intent, while deployment command delay and discontinuity differ from independent random training commands.
## Method

A single 29-dimensional policy learns velocity first, then height, torso, and arms while retaining prior skills. Quintic interpolation and randomized command release shape the deployment interface. Arm output is `q_final = q_desired + q_residual`; wrist loads and a CoM projection term train compensation.
## Key figures
![Figure 2: unified policy and sequential curriculum](../assets/ulc-2507.06905v2/figure-2-unified-policy.jpg)
The figure is a command protocol, not merely a larger observation vector.
![Tables III-IV and Figure 3: command-space evaluation](../assets/ulc-2507.06905v2/table-3-4-figure-3.jpg)
Command range and tracking precision are separate axes and should not be collapsed.
![Table V: mechanism ablation](../assets/ulc-2507.06905v2/table-5-ablation.jpg)
Removing sequential training, residual arms, or CoM tracking produces different failure modes, supporting distinct roles.
## Decisive evidence

Table V is more causal than the hardware demos: under 2 kg wrist loads, each removed component degrades the metric it is designed to protect. Real doll/refrigerator tasks show interface usability but lack complete trial denominators.
## Paper-to-implementation mapping

With no verified official code, an implementation must expose curriculum state/thresholds, command interpolation and delay queue, residual-arm composition, CoM target, action scaling, and the 50 Hz policy/PD interface. These are required audit surfaces, not claimed author symbols.
## Limits and evidence boundary

The paper reports one G1 morphology and mainly qualitative manipulation. The CoM proxy does not fully encode support polygons, and a unified network can propagate upper-body command faults into gait. No published parameters constitute a hardware permission set.
## Bounded engineering takeaway

Stage multi-objective learning and preserve explicit feedforward-versus-residual limits. Evaluate isolated commands, simultaneous commands, abrupt changes, delay, payload, and unreachable requests; reject invalid commands above the policy.
## Reproduction checklist

Lock curriculum progression, rewards, command ranges, interpolation, delay distribution, history, residual scaling, payloads, CoM term, PD, and rate. Report workspace and precision separately, plus fall, slip, torque, contact, thermal state, stage success, and intervention counts.
